buy3 blends 3 bonus tiers — "84x" and "97x" are both real, they're just different statistics. buy3 forces a Normal/Super/Hidden trigger and the RGS optimizer assigns each recorded outcome its own weight, so the tier breakdown above is each tier's own weighted mean as actually drawn within buy3 — not the raw per-drop reward table averaged in isolation. The overall buy3 mean is the weight-blend of all three. If your own script reports a different Normal-tier number, it's likely measuring the reward table directly (unweighted, outside buy3's RTP optimizer) rather than this in-context conditional mean — a different, equally real quantity, not a bug.
Each round is drawn from a 200-round pool, itself sampled uniformly (not by weight — that would bias the pool toward whichever few outcomes happen to carry outsized weight) from the real 20,000-sim buy3 library. "New Round" then draws among those 200 using their actual lookup-table weights (lookUpTable_buy3_0.csv) — the same odds a real RGS would use. Click it enough times and the session average (rounds played: 0) converges toward the pool's own mean, not the true 20,000-sim mean directly — a 200-round sample of a heavy right-tailed payout distribution (a few rare, very large wins account for a real share of the true mean) will itself land somewhat off from the full-library figure by ordinary sampling variance, same as any real finite play session would. That gap is honest, not an error in the player.
